issues.description: The template and problem statement require the pixel memory address to be calculated into ESI (and later pushed so it can be popped into a register and dereferenced: mov ecx, [esi]). The solution's main implementation, however, computes the offset into EDI (and leaves ESI as only display_start), performs incorrect arithmetic (adds 4 to edi before adding x*4) and never produces the full address in ESI. As a result the pushed value is just display_start (not display_start + offset) and the subsequent memory reads/writes will access the wrong location. This mismatches the explicit contract in the template/problem (result in ESI, then mov ecx,[esi]) and will confuse students and produce incorrect behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's main TODO implementation to compute the full pixel address into ESI (e.g. compute offset = (y * 1920 + x) * 4, add display_start and store result in ESI), then use mov ecx, [esi] and push esi. Alternatively, make the template and problem statements consistent with the solution by documenting that the computed address must be in EDI and updating all push/pop and dereference sites accordingly. Prefer the first fix to match the original template contract.
